subject: Mutual Action Plan: benchmarking discrepancies & repro timeline
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Evan Torres <evan.torres@contouranalytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Mutual Action Plan + benchmark results we discussed

Evan — following up with the MAP and the preliminary performance snapshot we ran against your sample workload. I attached the MAP spreadsheet (tabbed for milestones) and a short SLO summary. Key callouts:

- TTFT: median ~210ms on our Dedicated tier (p50 tokens-to-first-token, 32k context test).
- Sustained throughput: ~180 tokens/sec per GPU with our default batching policy for that model.
- Concurrency: we saw tail latency rising past 1.2s at 20 concurrent streams in this config.

We flagged a discrepancy vs the numbers you quoted from your in-house run — notably your TTFT is consistently ~120–140ms. Would like to understand what variables we should align on (client SDK, prompt prefix handling, tokenization differences, sequence length distribution, warm vs cold KV cache).

Next steps I propose: 1) quick sync to align test parameters, 2) share raw logs (I attached a small tar of latency traces), 3) mutually agree on an exact repro harness for the MAP so we can lock the close timeline. Are you available for a 30m call Wed or Thu?

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

Attachments: MAP_v1_Contour_RD-9742.xlsx (xlsx), latency_test_logs_20261028.tar.gz (tgz), slo-summary_contour.pdf (pdf)

Marissa — thanks for the quick turnaround and for the attachments.

We see the same pattern in our runs when using the open-source harness, but our internal service (wrapped with a lighter-weight gRPC client and a pre-tokenized request path) gets faster TTFT. Possible differences to check: tokenization (we use SentencePiece variant), whether Redwood's runs include prompt engineering layers (system message) in the measured tokens, and whether caching was warmed.

I'm available Thu 11:00–11:30 PT for a call. I uploaded our minimal trace and a pared-down HAR to the Drive link you provided.

Evan
Lead Platform Engineer, Contour Analytics
evant@contouranalytics.com

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-28T11:42:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: latency traces from Contour — quick triage notes

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding Evan's traces (they're in Drive). Quick notes from my local pass:

- Contour's traces show client-side batching disabled (single-request streams) which would lower observed TTFT at low qps but hurt throughput.
- Their tokenization uses SentencePiece and a custom pre-tokenization step which strips leading whitespace; that can shift token counts by ~5–8% on dev prompts we sampled.
- They appear to run with a warmed KV cache for long sessions in their prod harness; the first-call cold TTFT is not present in their reported numbers.

I recommend we: a) reproduce their exact client pipeline locally, b) instrument our inference runtime to record the same per-request markers (client_received, server_queued, started_compute), and c) run a 3x repeat with toggles for pre-tokenization and cache-warm.

-J
Jasmine Liu
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-29T08:55:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: latency traces from Contour — quick triage notes

All — I ran a quick matrix on our side to test a few hypotheses Jasmine raised. High level:

- When we replicate Contour's single-stream, pre-tokenized pipeline, our cold TTFT drops to ~130ms (closer to their number). Warmed sessions still provide ~180–200ms p50 when we include model startup overhead.
- The difference in token counts due to SentencePiece variant explains ~6% of throughput delta. That lines up with fewer tokens = fewer compute ops.
- Our batching policy (we default to a 4ms aggregation window) adds micro-latency at very low concurrency; switching to the zero-latency passthrough setting recovers ~20–30ms in TTFT for single-stream tests.

Implication for MAP: we should document precise client harness settings (tokenizer variant, batching window, warmup policy) as MAP milestones. Also recommend adding a 'competitive parity' sheet that shows how to align runs when customers compare against alternate vendors (kernel selection and quantization flags are frequent sources of mismatch).

I'll prepare a repro script and container with toggles for the above. ETA: Tue 2026-11-02.

-Karthik
Senior Benchmark Engineer

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Evan Torres <evan.torres@contouranalytics.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@contouranalytics.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-29T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan: benchmarking discrepancies & repro timeline

Evan — thanks for the trace upload and for confirming Thu morning. Quick alignment for the MAP milestones so we have a shared timeline:

1) By Tue 2026-11-02: Redwood provides a containerized repro harness (includes toggles for pre-tokenization, batching window, and cache-warm) + a README and test dataset. (owner: Karthik)
2) By Thu 2026-11-04: Contour runs the harness in their environment and shares raw logs; we will rerun in Redwood's Dedicated infra the same day.
3) By Mon 2026-11-09: Joint results sync with an action list: SLO adjustments, config changes, or alternate model variants.

We will also include a short appendix in the MAP that enumerates methodology differences and a 'competitive parity' checklist for external comparisons. If that timeline works, I'll lock these dates in the MAP spreadsheet and book the 11/09 sync.

Marissa

Marissa — that timeline looks reasonable. One note on the 11/02 run: we need the harness to include a reproducible random seed option and an option to pre-warm KV cache for N sessions. Also please confirm the exact model artifact: are we testing model v2.1-fp16-quant or v2.1-int8? Our in-house run used an int8 variant.

I'll confirm availability for the 11/09 sync after our internal bench run.

Best,
Priya
Head of Platform Engineering, Contour Analytics

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@contouranalytics.com>, Evan Torres <evan.torres@contouranalytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan: benchmarking discrepancies & repro timeline — harness delivered

All — attached is the container image ref and the repro script (pushed to the Drive folder). Summary of what the harness does and toggles:

- Tokenizer: options for default Redwood tokenizer or SentencePiece variant (seeded).
- Batching: aggregation window configurable (0ms, 2ms, 4ms).
- Cache warm: warm N sessions before measurement (0/10/50).
- Model: v2.1-fp16-quant (default) and v2.1-int8 (toggle).
- Deterministic seed support for request ordering and synthetic prompt sampling.

Initial internal runs (on Redwood Dedicated infra) using Contour's single-stream configuration: p50 TTFT ~128ms, p95 ~310ms at the single-session test. With batching window 4ms and cold cache the p50 shifts to ~210ms (matches Marissa's initial snapshot).

Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/rd-9742-bench
Container ref: ghcr.io/redwood-inference/rd-9742-harness:20261102

Next: Contour team runs this in their environment and drops logs in Drive. We will compare trace markers and prepare a short methodology appendix for the MAP that enumerates the exact flags we used.

-Karthik
